seo.title: FAQ — Tokenization Questions Answered
seo.description: Answers to common questions about Sereel, tokenization, blockchain settlement, custody, compliance, and institutional adoption of tokenized assets.

faq.lede: A short primer for institutional teams evaluating tokenisation infrastructure.

whatIsSereel.question: What is Sereel?
whatIsSereel.answer: Sereel provides institutional-grade infrastructure for the issuance, management, distribution and lifecycle administration of tokenised real-world assets and investment products. It helps regulated institutions, asset managers, issuers and investment platforms bring traditional financial products onto blockchain infrastructure while maintaining compliance, governance and investor protections. Sereel does not change the underlying asset — it modernises how ownership, transfers, reporting and settlement are managed.

whatIsTokenisation.question: What is tokenisation?
whatIsTokenisation.answer: Tokenisation is the process of representing ownership rights in a real-world asset or investment product as a secure digital record on blockchain infrastructure. Examples include real estate, private credit, money market funds, infrastructure projects, commodities, fixed income products, structured products and private equity interests. The underlying asset remains unchanged — tokenisation creates a more efficient framework for ownership and distribution.

doesTokenisationChangeValue.question: Does tokenisation change the value of an asset?
doesTokenisationChangeValue.answer: No. Tokenisation does not create value by itself. The value of a tokenised asset remains linked to the underlying asset, investment product or cash flow it represents. What changes is how ownership is recorded, transferred, administered and reported.

isCryptocurrencyPlatform.question: Is Sereel a cryptocurrency platform?
isCryptocurrencyPlatform.answer: No. Sereel is infrastructure for regulated financial products and real-world assets. While blockchain is used as the underlying technology, the focus is institutional investment infrastructure — not speculative cryptocurrency trading.

isIssuerOrSponsor.question: Is Sereel the issuer or asset sponsor?
isIssuerOrSponsor.answer: No. Sereel provides the rails for issuance, custody, compliance controls, settlement, subscriptions, redemptions and controlled transfers. The issuer owns the asset, disclosures, investor relationship, obligations and performance.

whoIsBuiltFor.question: Who is Sereel built for?
whoIsBuiltFor.answer: Sereel is designed for asset managers, fund managers, banks, issuers, investment platforms, family offices, institutional investors, real estate developers, private credit managers, distribution partners and compliance teams.

whyBlockchainForInvestments.question: Why use blockchain for investment products?
whyBlockchainForInvestments.answer: Traditional financial infrastructure can be slow, fragmented and heavily dependent on manual reconciliation. Blockchain enables faster settlement, better transparency, immutable ownership records, automated corporate actions, reduced administrative burden, stronger audit trails and broader accessibility. Sereel uses blockchain to improve infrastructure, not to replace legal and regulatory frameworks.

whyNotDatabase.question: Why not simply use a traditional database?
whyNotDatabase.answer: Traditional databases depend on a central party to maintain trust and reconcile records. Blockchain provides a shared source of truth that can be independently verified by multiple stakeholders — issuers, investors, custodians, administrators and regulators — all needing consistent records.

benefitOfInstantSettlement.question: What is the benefit of instant settlement?
benefitOfInstantSettlement.answer: Traditional securities settlement often takes multiple days. Blockchain-based settlement can allow ownership and payment to move together, reducing delay and counterparty risk. This improves capital efficiency, liquidity management, investor onboarding, operational speed and settlement certainty.

whyMultiChain.question: Why is Sereel multi-chain?
whyMultiChain.answer: No single blockchain fits every institution, market or use case. Sereel's multi-chain approach gives issuers access to different ecosystems, liquidity pools and investor communities while keeping the same compliance and governance logic across deployments.

whyMultiChainMattersForRwa.question: Why does multi-chain deployment matter for RWAs?
whyMultiChainMattersForRwa.answer: Multi-chain deployment helps issuers avoid dependence on one network and supports broader distribution and interoperability. It helps with investor reach, liquidity access, network resilience, ecosystem flexibility and future-proofing — especially as the tokenisation market continues to develop.

whichNetworksSupported.question: Which networks does Sereel support?
whichNetworksSupported.answer: Sereel supports all EVM-compatible chains, Solana, Canton, Bitcoin, IOTA, public blockchain networks, private blockchain environments and ZKsync Prividium deployments. Network selection depends on the product structure, custody model, privacy requirements, investor access and regulatory needs.

howAssetsSecured.question: How are tokenised assets secured?
howAssetsSecured.answer: Security is built in layers and may include institutional custody, multi-signature controls, multi-party computation (MPC), hardware security modules, role-based permissions, audit trails and governance controls. The design is intended to meet institutional expectations, not retail crypto standards.

whatIsMultiSig.question: What is multi-signature security?
whatIsMultiSig.answer: Multi-signature security requires more than one authorised approval before a transaction can proceed. This reduces single-point failure risk, internal fraud risk, operational errors and key compromise exposure.

whatIsMpcCustody.question: What is MPC custody?
whatIsMpcCustody.answer: MPC (multi-party computation) distributes cryptographic control without exposing a full private key in one place. That strengthens security while supporting controlled operations and recovery processes.

whatIfKeyLost.question: What happens if a private key is lost?
whatIfKeyLost.answer: Recovery procedures can be built into the custody and governance model, including multi-signature recovery, MPC recovery, backup signers, governance-approved recovery workflows and institutional custody support. Recovery terms should always be defined before issuance.

doesSereelCustodyAssets.question: Does Sereel custody client assets?
doesSereelCustodyAssets.answer: No. Custody remains with approved custodians, regulated providers or the designated legal structure for the product. Sereel provides infrastructure rather than taking ownership of investor assets.

whatIfSereelCeasesOperations.question: What happens if Sereel ceases operations?
whatIfSereelCeasesOperations.answer: Token records remain on-chain. Investor rights continue to be governed by the legal structure, transaction documents and the asset's governing terms — rather than by one software provider alone.

areTokenisedAssetsLegal.question: Are tokenised assets legal?
areTokenisedAssetsLegal.answer: In many jurisdictions, tokenised assets are recognised under existing securities, trust, property or investment laws. Tokenisation usually updates the ownership record and transfer process — it does not replace the legal rights attached to the asset.

howSereelSupportsCompliance.question: How does Sereel support compliance?
howSereelSupportsCompliance.answer: Sereel can support KYC checks, AML controls, investor whitelisting, jurisdiction restrictions, transfer restrictions, investor eligibility checks and compliance reporting. These controls can be embedded into the issuance and transfer process.

canEligibilityBeEnforced.question: Can investor eligibility rules be enforced?
canEligibilityBeEnforced.answer: Yes. Issuers can define rules such as accredited investor only, institutional only, geographic restrictions, holding period restrictions and investor concentration limits. Transfers can then be restricted automatically to qualified wallets and approved investors.

whoDeterminesJurisdiction.question: Who determines the governing jurisdiction?
whoDeterminesJurisdiction.answer: The issuer does. The legal structure, governing law and investor terms are established during issuance and remain enforceable independent of the blockchain layer.

whatAssetsCanBeTokenised.question: What kinds of assets can be tokenised?
whatAssetsCanBeTokenised.answer: Sereel may support a wide range of asset classes including real estate, private credit, funds, fixed income products, commodities, infrastructure assets, structured products, private equity interests, revenue-linked instruments and alternative investment products.

canFundsBeTokenised.question: Can traditional funds be tokenised?
canFundsBeTokenised.answer: Yes. Traditional funds, including private funds and other collective investment structures, can be represented through tokenised ownership records.

canTokenisationImproveLiquidity.question: Can tokenisation improve liquidity?
canTokenisationImproveLiquidity.answer: Potentially, yes. Tokenisation can support fractional ownership, smaller ticket sizes, broader investor access and secondary market participation. However, liquidity still depends on market demand, investor participation and the availability of compliant trading venues.

whatIsFractionalOwnership.question: What is fractional ownership?
whatIsFractionalOwnership.answer: Fractional ownership means an asset is divided into smaller ownership units. This can lower entry thresholds and make it easier for more investors to participate.

whatMakesInstitutionalGrade.question: What makes Sereel institutional-grade?
whatMakesInstitutionalGrade.answer: Sereel is designed around compliance-first architecture, secure custody integrations, governance controls, institutional settlement standards, API-based integrations, auditability, scalability and regulatory adaptability. The platform is intended for professional market participants and regulated use cases.

howIntegratesWithExistingSystems.question: How does Sereel integrate with existing systems?
howIntegratesWithExistingSystems.answer: Sereel can connect through APIs to existing systems such as fund administration platforms, transfer agents, custodians, banking systems, reporting tools, treasury systems and investment platforms — helping institutions adopt tokenisation without replacing their entire operating stack.

canBeWhiteLabelled.question: Can Sereel be white-labelled?
canBeWhiteLabelled.answer: Yes. Institutions can launch products under their own brand while Sereel provides the infrastructure behind the scenes.

howCorporateActionsManaged.question: How are corporate actions managed?
howCorporateActionsManaged.answer: Corporate actions can be automated through programmable workflows covering coupon payments, dividend distributions, interest payments, redemptions, maturity events and investor notifications — reducing manual work and improving consistency.

mainRisks.question: What are the main risks users should understand?
mainRisks.answer: Like any financial infrastructure, tokenisation carries risks including regulatory change, market liquidity limitations, technology failure, custody risk, smart contract risk and jurisdictional complexity. These risks should be clearly disclosed in offering and legal documents.

howUpgradesHandled.question: How are upgrades handled?
howUpgradesHandled.answer: Where applicable, upgrades should be governed through a clear approval process. Critical compliance and ownership rules should remain tightly controlled, with changes made only under defined governance procedures.

areTokensValidIfPlatformChanges.question: Are tokens still valid if the platform changes?
areTokensValidIfPlatformChanges.answer: Yes, provided the legal structure and issuance terms remain in place. The token is a record of ownership, but the enforceable rights come from the legal documentation behind the product.

whatIssuerNeedsToLaunch.question: What does an issuer need to launch a tokenised product?
whatIssuerNeedsToLaunch.answer: Typically, an issuer will need a defined asset or fund structure, legal and regulatory review, investor eligibility rules, custody and recovery design, a distribution plan, a reporting framework, governance approvals and a technical integration plan.

canSupportSimpleAndComplex.question: Can Sereel support both simple and complex products?
canSupportSimpleAndComplex.answer: Yes. Sereel can support simpler products such as single-asset issuance, as well as more complex structures involving fund administration, distribution rules, compliance logic and lifecycle events.

whatIsSereelBuilding.question: What is Sereel building?
whatIsSereelBuilding.answer: Sereel is building the institutional infrastructure layer for tokenised capital markets — connecting traditional finance and blockchain-based market infrastructure in a way that is compliant, secure and practical for real-world use.

seo.title: Privacy Policy
seo.description: How Sereel Technologies collects, uses, discloses, and safeguards information across our website, digital asset platform, APIs, and related services.

introduction.heading: 1. Introduction
introduction.body1: Sereel Technologies Inc. ("Sereel," "we," "us," or "our") is committed to protecting your privacy. This Privacy Policy explains how we collect, use, disclose, and safeguard your information when you access our website at https://sereel.com, our digital asset management platform, APIs, and related services (collectively, the "Services").
introduction.body2: By using our Services, you consent to the practices described in this Privacy Policy. If you do not agree, please do not use the Services.

account.label: Account Information:
account.text: Name, email address, company name, job title, and other registration details.

business.label: Business Information:
business.text: Entity name, jurisdiction of incorporation, business registration details, and authorized representative information for institutional clients.

communications.label: Communications:
communications.text: Information you provide when contacting us, submitting support requests, or communicating through the Services.

transaction.label: Transaction Data:
transaction.text: Records of digital asset transactions, token issuance details, and related operational data processed through our platform.

usage.label: Usage Data:
usage.text: Pages visited, features used, timestamps, referral URLs, and interaction patterns within the Services.

device.label: Device and Technical Data:
device.text: IP address, browser type and version, operating system, device identifiers, and general location information derived from your IP address.

log.label: Log Data:
log.text: Server logs, error reports, and performance data related to your use of the Services.

identity.label: Identity Verification Data:
identity.text1: We use third-party Know Your Customer (KYC) and Know Your Business (KYB) providers to verify user and entity identities as required by applicable regulations. These providers collect and process sensitive identity information (such as government-issued ID documents, biometric data, proof of address, and sanctions screening results) directly.
identity.boldNote: Sereel does not store sensitive identity documents or biometric data on our systems.
identity.text2: We receive only verification status, risk scores, and summary results necessary to maintain compliance records.

blockchain.label: Blockchain Data:
blockchain.text: Publicly available on-chain transaction data associated with wallet addresses used in connection with the Services.

analytics.label: Analytics Providers:
analytics.text: Aggregated and anonymized usage data from third-party analytics services.

use.heading: 3. How We Use Your Information
use.intro: We use the information we collect for the following purposes:

providing.label: Providing the Services:
providing.text: To operate, maintain, and improve our digital asset infrastructure and platform.

compliance.label: Compliance and Regulatory Obligations:
compliance.text: To meet applicable legal, regulatory, and licensing requirements, including anti-money laundering (AML), counter-terrorism financing (CTF), and sanctions screening obligations across the jurisdictions in which we operate.

identityVerification.label: Identity Verification:
identityVerification.text: To coordinate with third-party KYC/KYB providers to verify the identity and eligibility of users and their organizations.

security.label: Security:
security.text: To detect, prevent, and respond to fraud, unauthorized access, and other security incidents.

communications.label: Communications:
communications.text: To respond to inquiries, send service-related notifications, and provide customer support.

analytics.label: Analytics and Improvement:
analytics.text: To understand how the Services are used and to improve functionality, performance, and user experience.

legal.label: Legal Purposes:
legal.text: To enforce our Terms of Use, comply with legal obligations, and protect our rights and the rights of others.

sharing.heading: 4. How We Share Your Information
sharing.intro: We do not sell your personal information. We may share your information in the following circumstances:

serviceProviders.heading: 4.1 Third-Party Service Providers
serviceProviders.intro: We share information with trusted third-party providers who perform services on our behalf, including:

kyc.label: KYC/KYB Verification Providers:
kyc.text: To conduct identity verification and compliance screening. These providers operate under their own privacy policies and data processing agreements.

cloud.label: Cloud Infrastructure Providers:
cloud.text: For hosting, data storage, and computing services.

analytics.label: Analytics Providers:
analytics.text: For usage analytics and performance monitoring.

communication.label: Communication Providers:
communication.text: For email delivery and customer support tools.

serviceProviders.footer: All service providers are contractually obligated to use your information only for the purposes of providing services to Sereel and to maintain appropriate security measures.

legalDisclosure.heading: 4.2 Legal and Regulatory Disclosure
legalDisclosure.intro: We may disclose your information where required by law, regulation, legal process, or governmental request, including:

items.subpoenas: Responding to subpoenas, court orders, or regulatory inquiries
items.lawEnforcement: Cooperating with law enforcement or regulatory authorities in any jurisdiction where we operate

businessTransfers.heading: 4.3 Business Transfers
businessTransfers.body: In the event of a merger, acquisition, reorganization, or sale of assets, your information may be transferred as part of that transaction. We will provide notice before your information becomes subject to a different privacy policy.

consent.heading: 4.4 With Your Consent
consent.body: We may share your information with third parties when you have given us explicit consent to do so.

retention.heading: 5. Data Retention
retention.intro: We retain your information for as long as necessary to:

items.provide: Provide the Services and maintain your account
items.comply: Comply with legal, regulatory, and licensing obligations (including record-keeping requirements that may extend for several years after account closure)
items.resolve: Resolve disputes and enforce our agreements

retention.footer: When information is no longer needed for these purposes, we securely delete or anonymize it in accordance with our data retention policies.

security.heading: 6. Data Security
security.intro: We implement appropriate technical and organizational measures to protect your information, including:

items.encryption: Encryption of data in transit and at rest
items.standards: Compliance with industry standards including SOC 2 and ISO 27001 frameworks

security.footer: While we strive to protect your information, no method of electronic transmission or storage is completely secure. We cannot guarantee absolute security, but we are committed to maintaining industry-standard protections.

internationalTransfers.heading: 7. International Data Transfers
internationalTransfers.intro: Sereel operates across multiple jurisdictions, including the United States, Kenya, Nigeria, the Netherlands, and Botswana. Your information may be transferred to and processed in countries other than your country of residence. When we transfer data internationally, we implement appropriate safeguards, including:

items.scc: Standard contractual clauses or equivalent mechanisms approved by applicable data protection authorities
items.dpa: Data processing agreements with all third-party providers
items.compliance: Compliance with applicable data transfer regulations in each jurisdiction

rights.heading: 8. Your Rights

access.label: Access:
access.text: Request a copy of the personal information we hold about you.

correction.label: Correction:
correction.text: Request correction of inaccurate or incomplete information.

deletion.label: Deletion:
deletion.text: Request deletion of your personal information, subject to legal and regulatory retention requirements.

restriction.label: Restriction:
restriction.text: Request that we restrict processing of your information in certain circumstances.

portability.label: Portability:
portability.text: Request a portable copy of your information in a structured, commonly used format.

objection.label: Objection:
objection.text: Object to processing of your information for certain purposes.

withdrawConsent.label: Withdraw Consent:
withdrawConsent.text: Where processing is based on consent, you may withdraw consent at any time.

rights.contact: To exercise any of these rights, please contact us at privacy@sereel.com. We will respond to your request within the timeframe required by applicable law.
rights.limitation: Please note that certain rights may be limited where we have a legal obligation to retain data, particularly in connection with regulatory compliance, AML/CTF requirements, or ongoing investigations.

cookies.intro: We may use cookies and similar tracking technologies to collect usage data and improve the Services. These may include:

essential.label: Essential Cookies:
essential.text: Required for the operation of the Services.

analytics.label: Analytics Cookies:
analytics.text: Used to understand how visitors interact with the Services.

preference.label: Preference Cookies:
preference.text: Used to remember your settings and preferences.

cookies.footer: You can manage cookie preferences through your browser settings. Disabling certain cookies may affect the functionality of the Services.

childrensPrivacy.body: Our Services are not directed to individuals under the age of 18 (or the applicable age of majority in your jurisdiction). We do not knowingly collect personal information from children. If we become aware that we have collected information from a child, we will take steps to delete it promptly.

thirdPartyLinks.body: The Services may contain links to third-party websites, services, or applications. We are not responsible for the privacy practices of these third parties. We encourage you to review the privacy policies of any third-party services you access through our platform.

changes.heading: 12. Changes to This Privacy Policy
changes.body1: We may update this Privacy Policy from time to time. We will notify you of material changes by posting the updated policy on our website and updating the "Last Updated" date. We may also provide additional notice for significant changes, such as email notification to account holders.
changes.body2: Your continued use of the Services after changes are posted constitutes acceptance of the revised Privacy Policy.

dpo.heading: 13. Data Protection Officer
dpo.intro: For privacy-related inquiries, concerns, or to exercise your data protection rights, please contact:

eeaUk.heading: European Economic Area (EEA) and United Kingdom
eeaUk.intro: If you are located in the EEA or UK, we process your personal data under the following legal bases as defined by the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR):

contract.label: Contract Performance:
contract.text: Processing necessary to provide the Services you have requested.

legalObligation.label: Legal Obligation:
legalObligation.text: Processing required to comply with applicable laws and regulations.

legitimateInterests.label: Legitimate Interests:
legitimateInterests.text: Processing necessary for our legitimate business interests, including security, fraud prevention, and service improvement, where these interests are not overridden by your rights.

consent.label: Consent:
consent.text: Where you have provided explicit consent for specific processing activities.

aboutServices.intro: Sereel provides blockchain-based digital asset infrastructure and capital markets technology services for institutional clients, including but not limited to:

bullets.tokenization: Tokenization of real-world assets using compliant smart contract standards (e.g., ERC-3643)
bullets.issuance: Digital securities issuance and lifecycle management
bullets.compliance: Compliance engine services for regulated digital assets
bullets.api: API access for integration with client platforms and systems

aboutServices.outro: Our Services are designed for institutional and professional use, including funds, asset managers, and financial intermediaries.

irreversible.body: Once a transaction is confirmed on a blockchain network, it generally cannot be reversed or undone.

volatile.body: The value of tokenized assets and digital securities may fluctuate significantly.

regulatory.body: The legal and regulatory landscape for digital assets varies by jurisdiction and is evolving. Compliance requirements may change.

smartContracts.body: While we employ rigorous compliance standards, smart contracts may contain vulnerabilities or behave unexpectedly under certain conditions.

network.body: Blockchain networks may experience congestion, forks, or other disruptions beyond our control.
